meta.name: Jalapeño Cheddar Sourdough - 67% Hydration
meta.description: Enriched sourdough with milk powder, butter, and brown sugar — soft sandwich-style crumb studded with fresh jalapeño heat and melty cheddar pockets. 66% base hydration (67% effective with butter), 61% inclusion load by baker's weight. Inclusions contribute ~192g moisture — shape fast before they bleed. Inspired by Proof Bread's Ukrainian baton-style approach.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe from Proof Bread YouTube video + multi-agent research synthesis (8 agents, 50+ sources)

states.title: Build & Ferment Levain
states.direction: In a clean glass jar, combine 50g bread flour, 50g water, and 10g ripe sourdough starter. Mix until no dry flour remains. Cover loosely and ferment at 74-76°F (23-24°C) for 10-12 hours.
states.exit_condition: Levain has doubled in volume, is domed on top, and smells pleasantly yeasty-sour. A small spoonful floats in water.

notes.text: Build the evening before bake day. If your kitchen is cool (below 68°F / 20°C), use slightly warmer water to compensate.

states.title: Autolyse Rest
states.direction: In a large mixing bowl, combine 500g bread flour and 310g water. Mix until no dry flour remains. Place all 110g of ripe levain on top of the dough (do not mix in yet). Cover and rest 20-30 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough is shaggy but fully hydrated with no dry pockets. Levain sits on top, untouched.

notes.text: Place starter on top of autolyse immediately — this prevents forgetting it later. Proof Bread uses this habit to avoid accidentally omitting the starter.
Use this rest time to prep jalapeños and cube cheddar (next two steps run in parallel).
Try: Skip levain build entirely — use 100g active starter in place of the 110g levain. Adjust flour/water totals to compensate for the 50g/50g no longer in levain.

states.title: Dice Jalapeños
states.direction: Wearing disposable gloves, stem and halve jalapeños. Remove seeds for milder heat or leave them for full spice. Dice into 5-8mm pieces. Weigh out 60g per loaf (120g total).
states.exit_condition: Jalapeños diced uniformly, seeds removed to preference, weighed and staged in a bowl.

notes.text: Always use gloves — capsaicin lingers on hands for hours and will burn eyes or contacts later.
Fresh jalapeños deliver sharper heat and more vibrant color than pickled. If substituting pickled, drain thoroughly and squeeze out all excess brine to prevent moisture issues.

states.title: Cube Cheddar
states.direction: Cut block cheddar into 1cm cubes. Slice block into 1cm slabs, then cut into 1cm strips, then crosscut into cubes. Weigh out 110g per loaf (220g total).
states.exit_condition: Cheddar cubed uniformly at ~1cm, weighed and staged. Cubes will clump together — that is normal for block cheese without cellulose.

notes.text: Always cube from a block — never use pre-shredded. Pre-shredded cheese is coated with cellulose anti-caking agent that prevents proper melting and creates a webbing effect that restricts dough expansion.
Sharp or extra-sharp cheddar provides the best flavor contrast. 1cm cubes melt into distinct pockets without dissolving into the dough.

states.title: Pre-Mix Dry Additions
states.direction: In a medium bowl, combine 10g salt, 25g milk powder, and 28g brown sugar. Mix by hand, breaking up any brown sugar clumps. Discard any hard crystallized sugar pieces.
states.exit_condition: Dry additions evenly combined with no hard brown sugar clumps remaining.

notes.text: Pre-mixing prevents brown sugar from clumping in the dough. Crystallized pieces survive fermentation and create sugary pockets in the crumb.

Milk powder is used instead of liquid milk because liquid milk contains glutathione, an enzyme that attacks gluten bonds during long sourdough fermentation. Milk powder is heat-treated to deactivate it.

states.title: Incorporate Levain & Dry Mix
states.direction: Squeeze the levain into the autolysed dough. Add the dry pre-mix (salt, milk powder, brown sugar) on top. Using wet hands, pinch and fold the dough until all additions are fully incorporated, 3-5 minutes.
states.exit_condition: No streaks of levain visible, dry additions fully dissolved into dough. Dough feels cohesive but not yet smooth.

states.title: Develop Gluten
states.direction: Using slap-and-fold technique on a clean counter, work the dough for 5-8 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and passes a gentle windowpane test.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth and elastic. A small piece stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing (windowpane test).

notes.text: Do NOT add butter yet. Gluten must be well-developed first — fat coats gluten proteins and prevents cross-linking if added too early.

states.title: Add Butter
states.direction: With the dough on the counter, smear 45g room-temperature butter across the surface. Fold the dough over the butter and continue working it in by pinching, folding, and kneading for 3-5 minutes until fully incorporated.
states.exit_condition: Butter fully incorporated — no visible streaks or slick patches. Dough is smooth and slightly tacky.

notes.text: The dough will feel greasy and fall apart initially. Keep working it — the gluten network re-forms around the fat within a few minutes.

states.title: Fold In Inclusions
states.direction: Flatten the dough on the counter. Spread jalapeños and cheddar cubes in an even layer across the surface. Fold the dough over the inclusions like a letter (thirds). Rotate 90° and fold again. Repeat 2-3 times until inclusions are roughly distributed. Transfer to a lightly oiled container for bulk fermentation.
states.exit_condition: Inclusions distributed throughout the dough in visible layers. Perfect uniformity not required — subsequent folds will even them out.

notes.text: This lamination technique preserves dough structure and distributes cheese and peppers in pockets rather than dissolving them into the dough.
Some cheese will fall out during folding — that is normal with cubes. Push stray pieces back in.

states.title: Stretch & Fold + Rest (Set 2)
states.direction: With wet hands, perform one set of stretch and folds — pull dough up from each of the four sides and fold over the center. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough feels stronger and more cohesive. Inclusions are more evenly distributed than after first fold.

states.title: Stretch & Fold + Rest (Set 3)
states.direction: Perform another set of stretch and folds from all four sides. Handle gently — the dough should be gaining strength and airiness. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough is noticeably puffier, smoother on the surface, and holds its shape when folded.

states.title: Stretch & Fold + Rest (Set 4)
states.direction: Final set of gentle stretch and folds. If dough resists stretching, skip this set — it has enough strength. Cover and rest.
states.exit_condition: Dough is strong, jiggly, and holds a dome shape. Inclusions are well distributed throughout.

notes.text: If the dough feels very tight and resists stretching, skip this fold. Over-developing an enriched dough with heavy inclusions can tear the gluten network.

states.title: Bulk Rest
states.direction: Leave the dough covered at 75-80°F (24-27°C) until it has risen 50-75% in volume. The surface should be domed with visible bubbles on the sides of the container.
states.exit_condition: Dough has risen 50-75% from its post-fold volume. Surface is domed, edges show visible bubbles. Total bulk fermentation time (including folds): 4-6 hours at 75-80°F (24-27°C).

notes.text: Enriched dough ferments slower than lean sourdough. Insufficient bulk fermentation is the primary cause of flat loaves with this bread.
At 68-72°F (20-22°C), bulk may take 6-8 hours. At 80°F+ (27°C+), it may only need 3-4 hours. Judge by volume, not time.

states.title: Divide Dough
states.direction: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Using a bench scraper, divide into two equal pieces, each approximately 690g.
states.exit_condition: Two roughly equal pieces of dough, each ~690g.

states.title: Preshape
states.direction: Using a bench scraper and minimal flour, gently shape each piece into a loose round. Pull the dough toward you on the counter to build light surface tension. Do not degas aggressively.
states.exit_condition: Two loose rounds with light surface tension sitting on the counter.

states.title: Bench Rest
states.direction: Leave preshaped rounds uncovered on the counter for 20-30 minutes. The dough should relax and spread slightly but still hold a rounded shape.
states.exit_condition: Dough has relaxed enough to shape easily — it spreads slightly but does not flatten. Pressing gently leaves a slow-recovering indent.

states.title: Final Shape (Batard)
states.direction: Working with one piece at a time: flip the round seam-side up. Fold the top third down and press to seal. Fold the bottom third up and over, pressing to seal. Roll the dough tightly into a log, stretching the skin taut as you go. Pinch the seam closed. Place seam-side up into a floured banneton.
states.exit_condition: Two tight, elongated batards with taut skin, seam-side down on parchment. No loose flaps or weak spots in the surface.

notes.text: Shape as batards, NOT rounds. Proof Bread identified that stopping at the preshape round (skipping final batard shaping) is a primary cause of flat loaves.
Build strong surface tension — the tighter the shape, the better the loaf holds up during proof and bake. Think of stretching the dough skin like a tight burrito.

Alternative: proof seam-side down on a parchment-lined sheet tray instead of a banneton. Avoids jalapeño and cheese oils permanently scenting your proofing baskets. Use a banneton liner if you want the ring pattern without the smell. Or dedicate a banneton for inclusion breads — the seasoning is harmless.

Try: Loaf pan variation — skip batard shaping entirely, place ~690g dough into a greased 9×5 loaf pan. Cold retard in the pan, bake covered with foil 25 min then uncovered 20 min at 425°F (218°C). Produces a sandwich-style jalapeño cheddar pullman.
Some cheddar cubes will poke through the surface. That is expected and creates attractive caramelized cheese patches during baking.

states.title: Cold Retard
states.direction: Cover each banneton tightly with plastic wrap or a shower cap. Refrigerate at 38-40°F (3-4°C) for 12-16 hours overnight.
states.exit_condition: Loaves have puffed slightly but still feel firm and cold. They should pass the poke test with very slow recovery (slight underproof is ideal for this bread).

notes.text: Cold retard develops flavor (sour tang) and makes the dough easier to score. Bake straight from the fridge — do not warm up.
Bannetons fit in the fridge more easily than a full sheet tray. If using sheet tray method instead, cover tightly with plastic wrap.

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Place Dutch oven with lid inside your oven. Preheat to 450°F (230°C) for 45-60 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Oven and Dutch oven have been at 450°F (230°C) for at least 45 minutes.

states.title: Score
states.direction: Remove one loaf from the fridge. Using a bread lame held at a 30-45° angle, make one confident, deep slash (~1.3cm deep) along the length of the loaf. Transfer immediately to the preheated Dutch oven using the parchment as a sling.
states.exit_condition: One deep, clean score running the length of the batard. The cut opens slightly, revealing the dough underneath.

notes.text: Score cold dough straight from the fridge — it holds shape and the blade cuts cleanly. One deep functional score is ideal for cheese bread; complex patterns risk fusing shut when cheese melts.

states.title: Bake (Steam Phase)
states.direction: Place the lid on the Dutch oven. Bake at 450°F (230°C) for 30 minutes with the lid on.
states.exit_condition: 30 minutes elapsed. Do not open the lid during this phase.

states.title: Bake (Dry Phase)
states.direction: Carefully remove the Dutch oven lid. Continue baking at 450°F (230°C) for 15-20 minutes until the crust is deep golden brown and the internal temperature reads 205°F (96°C).
states.exit_condition: Crust is deep golden brown with caramelized cheese patches. Internal temperature reads 205°F (96°C) or above. The loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.

notes.text: Home ovens need a higher internal temp target (205°F / 96°C) than commercial rack ovens (190-200°F) because steam dissipates once the lid comes off.
If the crust is browning too fast but internal temp is low, drop oven to 425°F (218°C) and extend baking.

states.title: Cool
states.direction: Transfer the loaf to a wire cooling rack. Cool for at least 1 hour before cutting. Repeat the scoring and baking process for the second loaf.
states.exit_condition: Loaf has cooled to the point where the crumb has set — the center no longer feels hot to the touch.

notes.text: The crumb continues to gelatinize during cooling. Cutting early releases steam that the crumb needs to set properly.

technical_notes.title: Levain vs. Active Starter
technical_notes.text:
- Recipe builds a dedicated **levain** (50g flour + 50g water + 10g starter) for precise fermentation control
- **To skip levain**: use 100g active, recently-fed starter instead
- Reduce dough flour by 40g and dough water by 40g to compensate
- **Trade-off**: lose independent timing from starter feed schedule; fresh levain's lower inoculation rate produces milder, more complex sourness

technical_notes.title: Hydration Analysis
technical_notes.text:
- **Base hydration**: 330g water ÷ 500g flour = **66%**
- **Butter**: ~13g water (16% moisture)
- **Levain**: ~50g water contribution
- **Milk powder**: ~0g (dry)
- **Effective hydration**: ~393g total water ÷ 550g total flour = **~71%**
- **Jalapeños**: ~90% water = ~68g moisture
- **Cheddar**: ~37% water = ~43g moisture
- **Total inclusion moisture**: ~111g — releases unevenly during bake, not part of gluten matrix
- Shape fast before inclusions bleed

methods.detail: Preheat to 350°F (175°C). Wrap loaf loosely in foil. Heat 10-15 minutes until warmed through. Unwrap for last 2 minutes to re-crisp crust.
Slice and toast at medium setting until edges are golden and cheese pockets begin to re-melt.

cook_log.summary: First bake — skipped levain, used active starter with adjusted flour/water (-40g each). Cold bulk fermented overnight instead of cold retard, shaped and proofed at room temp. Loaf 2 had better spring and smoother skin at lower temps (475/440 vs 480). Friend called it best bread yet.
notes: Skipped levain build — used active starter directly, reduced flour by 40g and water by 40g
Kitchen temp 75.9°F at autolyse start (10:15pm May 2)
DDT 78.4°F after butter — unsure about butter technique, may need to rewatch video
Did two stretch-and-fold sets, then switched to coil folds (lift in center and fold over itself)
Cold bulk fermented overnight in fridge (~2:22am to ~3:37pm, ~13 hrs). Dough still quite chilled at divide
Total dough weight 1390g, 695g target per loaf
Reversed recipe: cold bulk instead of cold retard. Shaped, then proofed room temp during preheat (~70 min loaf 1, ~2.5 hrs loaf 2)
Loaf 1: 480°F covered 20 min, 480°F uncovered ~20 min. Internal 210°F+
Loaf 2: 475°F covered 20 min, 440°F uncovered ~18 min. More spring, smoother skin, fluffier. Lower temps were better
Friend reports best bread yet. Took liberties due to time constraints — should always start these earlier
